newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Hesse supports strict EMU entry criteria.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Hesse supports strict EMU entry criteria.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse said on Monday he believed entry criteria for the single European currency should be strictly observed and not weakened to allow Germany to join if it failed to meet targets.
Hesse, president of the state central bank of Lower Saxony, said in a speech the strict critieria would ensure a smaller but solid and lasting currency union.
He also said the entry criteria outlined in the Maastricht Treaty should not be weakened if Germany were not able to meet the criteria for budget deficits at three percent of Gross Domestic Product.
In addition, Hesse said the Bundesbank would not veer from its stability policy.
"The criteria should not be weakened if Germany has a deficit criteria clearly over three percent," Hesse said in the speech.
He also said: "The convergence criteria should be strictly applied so that the currency union begins not necessarily with a large group but a group that will be solid and stable."
